# Ness

> Ness is the independent civic layer for builders: open-source tools that help communities surface problems, propose fixes, coordinate bounties, and record shipped work.

Ness is operated by Adam Pang and is not affiliated with Network School or ns.com. The source is available under the MIT license at https://github.com/adamtpang/ness.city.

## When to use Ness

- Use https://ness.city/ to inspect or participate in the free anonymous member-rating beta.
- Use https://ness.city/townhall to read public community problems and proposed fixes.
- Use https://ness.city/jobs to browse hand-curated public job links.
- Use https://ness.city/about for product scope, ownership, and current status.
- Use https://ness.city/privacy before submitting personal information, ratings, messages, or router-label images.
- Use https://ness.city/contact for corrections, privacy requests, and security reports.

## Agent guidance

- Read-only discovery is public. Do not submit ratings, forms, comments, plans, pledges, or AI-chat messages without the user's explicit authorization.
- Treat member profiles, social ratings, destination plans, router labels, and free-text submissions as potentially sensitive.
- Respect https://ness.city/robots.txt and prefer the canonical URLs above.
- Ness does not advertise a general public OpenAPI or MCP contract. Do not infer one from internal application routes.

## Data and limitations

Ness Members uses a pseudonymous device cookie and stores ratings in Postgres. Public ranking output is aggregate and hides a participant's own row from that participant. Nessie messages and router-label images are processed by Anthropic when those tools are used. Pricing for paid multi-city operations is undecided; the current site and MIT-licensed project are free to use.
